title: Economic Takeaways From the Trump-Xi Summit and Why It Matters for New Zealand
text:
Economic Takeaways From the Trump-Xi Summit and Why It Matters for New Zealand

NBR

Saul Loeb/AFP/Getty Images

The following is an excerpt from an op-ed published in NBR on October 3, 2026, written by Jane Mellsop, ASPI's Director of Trade, Investment, and Economic Security. Last week's meeting of the leaders of the world's two largest economies in Washington DC was short on substance but was nevertheless celebrated by both sides as confirming a relationship of 'constructive strategic stability' between the US and China. For New Zealand, the stability in the US-China trade and economic relationship — achieved through a short extension to the trade truce, the launch of a new AI dialogue, and agreement on the framework and mandate for their Board of Trade — is welcome news. However, the summit delivered largely process gains, and tensions around chip exports and access to rare earths magnets continue to bubble just below the surface and threaten the fragile truce. With exports making up close to a quarter of New Zealand's GDP, and China and the US holding first and second place in the list of New Zealand's top export markets, averting a trade war between these two partners is critical for New Zealand. Read the full op-ed here.
